module pe
(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [31:0] a,
    input [31:0] b,
    output reg [31:0] c
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            c <= 32'b0;
        end else begin
            c <= c + (a * b);
        end
    end
endmodule

    <description>Parallel-to-Serial Conversion Module</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal; active low.</input>
        <input id="d" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit parallel data input.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Valid signal indicating the availability of serial output.</output>
        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <!-- No parameter description needed for this module -->
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="cnt" width_description="[1:0]" initial_value="2'b00">
            <description>Counter register for tracking the current bit position during conversion.</description>
            <update_condition>On each clock edge.</update_condition>
            <update_expression>cnt + 1</update_expression>
        </register>
        <register id="data" width_description="[3:0]" initial_value="4'b0000">
            <description>Data register to hold the parallel data being converted.</description>
            <update_condition>When cnt reaches 3.</update_condition>
            <update_expression>d</update_expression>
        </register>
        <register id="valid" width_description="[0:0]" initial_value="1'b0">
            <description>Valid signal register to indicate the availability of serial output.</description>
            <update_condition>On each clock edge.</update_condition>
            <update_expression>valid ? 1'b0 : 1'b1</update_expression>
        </register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Assigning the most significant bit of the data register to the serial output
        assign dout = data[3];
        
        // Sequential logic for updating the data register based on the counter value
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                // Reset condition
                cnt <= 2'b00;
                data <= 4'b0000;
                valid <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt == 2'b11) begin
                    // Update data register with parallel input when cnt reaches 3
                    data <= d;
                    cnt <= 2'b00;
                    valid <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    // Increment counter and update valid signal
                    cnt <= cnt + 1;
                    valid <= 1'b0;
                    
                    // Shift data register left by 1 bit
                    data <= {data[2:0], data[3]};
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="fixed_point_adder">
    <description>A parameterizable fixed-point adder for performing arithmetic operations with specified precision.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[N-1:0]">First N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[N-1:0]">Second N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <output id="c" width_description="[N-1:0]">N-bit output representing the result of the fixed-point addition.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="Q">Number of fractional bits (precision).</parameter>
        <parameter id="N">Total number of bits, including integer and fractional parts.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="res" width_description="[N-1:0]">Register to store the result of the addition or subtraction.</register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Internal signals
        reg [N-1:0] abs_a;
        reg [N-1:0] abs_b;
        reg [N-1:0] temp_result;
        
        // Determine absolute values based on sign bits
        always @(*) begin
            if (a[N-1] == b[N-1]) begin
                // Both numbers have the same sign
                abs_a = a[N-1] ? -a : a; // Take absolute value of a
                abs_b = b[N-1] ? -b : b; // Take absolute value of b
                
                // Perform addition
                temp_result = abs_a + abs_b;
                
                // Set the sign bit of the result
                res = a[N-1] ? -temp_result : temp_result;
            end else begin
                // Numbers have different signs
                if (abs_a > abs_b) begin
                    // a is greater than b
                    temp_result = abs_a - abs_b;
                    
                    // Set the sign bit of the result
                    res = a[N-1] ? -temp_result : temp_result;
                end else begin
                    // b is greater than a
                    temp_result = abs_b - abs_a;
                    
                    // Set the sign bit of the result
                    res = b[N-1] ? -temp_result : temp_result;
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Output assignment
        assign c = res;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="freq_divbyfrac">
    <description>A frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency by fractional values. It generates a clock signal with a fractional frequency division (3.5x), using the double-edge clocking technique to achieve half-integer division while adjusting for duty cycle imbalance. By dividing uneven clock cycles and phase-shifting them, a smooth fractional clock output is produced.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Input clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active low reset signal to initialize the module.</input>
        <output id="clk_div">Fractionally divided clock output.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>The module performs fractional frequency division by counting clock cycles and generating an intermediate divided clock signal. For 3.5x division:</implementation>
    <implementation>The counter cycles through 7 clock cycles (MUL2_DIV_CLK = 7).</implementation>
    <implementation>It generates two uneven clock periods: one with 4 source clock cycles and another with 3 source clock cycles.</implementation>
    <implementation>In the next cycle, phase-shifted versions of the divided clock are generated. One phase is delayed by half a clock period, and the other is advanced by half a clock period.</implementation>
    <implementation>Finally, the two intermediate clocks are logically OR-ed to produce the final fractional divided clock output, ensuring the divided clock signal has a uniform period.</implementation>
</module>

    <description>An instruction register module designed to hold and process CPU instructions. It captures incoming instructions from various sources and separates them into distinct fields for further processing.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="rst">Active low reset signal to initialize the register.</input>
        <input id="fetch" width_description="[1:0]">Control signal indicating the source of the instruction (1 for register, 2 for RAM/ROM).</input>
        <input id="data" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit data input representing the instruction to be fetched.</input>
        <output id="ins" width_description="[2:0]">High 3 bits of the instruction, indicating the opcode or operation.</output>
        <output id="ad1" width_description="[4:0]">Low 5 bits of the instruction, representing the register address.</output>
        <output id="ad2" width_description="[7:0]">The full 8-bit data from the second source.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>The instruction register contains two 8-bit registers (ins_p1 and ins_p2) to store instructions from different sources. On the rising edge of the clock (clk), if the reset (rst) signal is low, both registers are initialized to zero. Based on the fetch signal, if fetch is 2'b01, the instruction is fetched from the data input into ins_p1. If fetch is 2'b10, the instruction is fetched from the data input into ins_p2. If neither condition is met, the previous values in both registers are retained. The outputs ins, ad1, and ad2 are derived from the stored instructions.</implementation>
</module>

        <parameter id="SRA">6'b000011</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLLV">6'b000100</parameter>

        <assign id="signed_b" width_description="[31:0]">Signed version of operand B.</assign>
        <assign id="res" width_description="[32:0]">Register to store the result of the operation.</assign>
        <assign id="shift_amount" width_description="[4:0]">Shift amount for shift operations.</assign>
        <always_comb>
            // Assigning values to signed_a and signed_b
            assign signed_a = $signed(a);
            assign signed_b = $signed(b);
            
            // Assigning values to res based on aluc
            always @(*) begin
                case(aluc)
                    ADD: res = signed_a + signed_b;
                    ADDU: res = a + b;
                    SUB: res = signed_a - signed_b;
                    SUBU: res = a - b;
                    AND: res = a & b;
                    OR: res = a | b;
                    XOR: res = a ^ b;

    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>

        <output id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">Generated waveform signal.</output>

        </register>

        // State and wave registers
        reg [4:0] wave;
        reg state;
        // Always block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or falling edge of the reset signal
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Reset condition
                state <= 1'b0; // Initialize state to 0
                wave <= 5'd0;  // Initialize wave to 0

                        wave <= wave + 1; // Increment wave value
                        if (wave == 5'd31) begin
                            state <= 1'b1; // Transition to state 1 when wave reaches maximum value
                        end
                    end
                    1'b1: begin
                        wave <= wave - 1; // Decrement wave value
                        if (wave == 5'd0) begin
                            state <= 1'b0; // Transition back to state 0 when wave reaches minimum value
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end

    </ports>
    <implementation>The barrel shifter shifts the input 'in' based on the value of the 'ctrl' signal. The shifting happens in stages, where each stage shifts by 4, 2, or 1 position, as controlled by 'ctrl[2]', 'ctrl[1]', and 'ctrl[0]' respectively. The shifts are achieved using a series of 2-to-1 multiplexers ('mux2X1') that select between the shifted input and the original input. <module id="freq_diveven">
    <description>Frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency by even numbers. This module generates a divided clock signal by toggling its output every specified number of input clock cycles.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Input clock signal that will be divided.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal to initialize the module.</input>
        <output id="clk_div">Divided clock output signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="NUM_DIV">The division factor for the frequency divider, must be an even number.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <signal id="cnt" width_description="[3:0]">Counter to track the number of clock cycles.</signal>
        <signal id="half_num_div_minus_one">Half of NUM_DIV minus one.</signal>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Initialize counter and divided clock signal
        cnt <= 4'd0;
        clk_div <= 1'b0;
        
        // Calculate half of NUM_DIV minus one
        half_num_div_minus_one = NUM_DIV / 2 - 1;
        
        // Counting mechanism
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 4'd0;
                clk_div <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt < half_num_div_minus_one) begin
                    cnt <= cnt + 1;
                end else begin
                    cnt <= 4'd0;
                    clk_div <= ~clk_div;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

    <description>A linear feedback shift register (LFSR) for generating pseudo-random sequences. This 4-bit LFSR uses a specific feedback mechanism to produce a sequence of bits that appears random.</description>

On the rising edge of the clock (clk), if the reset (rst) is high, the register is initialized to zero. Otherwise, the bits in the register are shifted left, and the new feedback value is inserted at the least significant bit (LSB).</implementation>
</module>

    <ports>
        <input id="dataIn" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit input data to be pushed onto the buffer.</input>
        <input id="RW">Read/Write control signal (1 for read, 0 for write).</input>

        <input id="Rst">Active high reset signal to initialize the buffer.</input>
        <input id="Clk">Clock signal for synchronous operations.</input>
        <output id="EMPTY">Flag indicating whether the buffer is empty.</output>
        <output id="FULL">Flag indicating whether the buffer is full.</output>
        <output id="dataOut" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit output data retrieved from the buffer.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>The buffer uses a stack memory array (stack_mem) to store the data. A stack pointer (SP) tracks the current position in the stack. On the rising edge of the clock (Clk), if the enable (EN) signal is high, the buffer checks if it is full or empty and processes data accordingly. If RW is low (write operation) and the buffer is not full, data from dataIn is pushed onto the stack, and the stack pointer is decremented. If RW is high (read operation) and the buffer is not empty, data is popped from the stack into dataOut, the corresponding stack memory is cleared, and the stack pointer is incremented. Flags for EMPTY and FULL are updated based on the stack pointer status.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Implement an 8-bit multiplier with pipelined processing stages.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal for multiplication.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplicand input with a width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplier input with a width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating multiplication operation status.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output with a width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description></parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic"></logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Input Enable Signal
        reg [1:0] mul_en_out_reg;
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_en_out_reg <= 2'b00;
            end else begin
                mul_en_out_reg[0] <= mul_en_in;
                mul_en_out_reg[1] <= mul_en_out_reg[0];
            end
        end
        assign mul_en_out = mul_en_out_reg[1];
        // Input Registers
        reg [7:0] mul_a_reg;
        reg [7:0] mul_b_reg;
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_a_reg <= 8'b0;
                mul_b_reg <= 8'b0;
            end else begin
                if (mul_en_in) begin
                    mul_a_reg <= mul_a;
                    mul_b_reg <= mul_b;
                end
            end
        end
        // Partial Product Generation
        wire [7:0] temp[7:0];
        genvar i;
        generate
            for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) begin : pp_gen
                assign temp[i] = mul_b_reg[i] ? (mul_a_reg << i) : 8'b0;
            end
        endgenerate
        // Partial Sum Calculation
        reg [15:0] sum[7:0];
        integer j;
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                for (j = 0; j < 8; j = j + 1) begin
                    sum[j] <= 16'b0;
                end
            end else begin
                for (j = 0; j < 8; j = j + 1) begin
                    sum[j] <= temp[j] + sum[j];
                end
            end
        end
        // Final Product Calculation
        reg [15:0] mul_out_reg;
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_out_reg <= 16'b0;
            end else begin
                mul_out_reg <= sum[0] + sum[1] + sum[2] + sum[3] +
                               sum[4] + sum[5] + sum[6] + sum[7];
            end
        end
        // Output Assignment
        assign mul_out = mul_en_out ? mul_out_reg : 16'b0;
    </implementation>

</module>

    <ports>

        <output id="clk_div">Divided clock output.</output>
    </ports>

        <parameter id="NUM_DIV" type="integer" default_value="5">Odd divisor value for frequency division.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <signal id="cnt1" type="reg" width="NUM_DIV-1" description="Counter for tracking rising edge clock cycles."/>
        <signal id="cnt2" type="reg" width="NUM_DIV-1" description="Counter for tracking falling edge clock cycles."/>
        <signal id="clk_div1" type="wire" description="Divided clock output for positive edge."/>
        <signal id="clk_div2" type="wire" description="Divided clock output for negative edge."/>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Counter for tracking rising edge clock cycles
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                cnt1 <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt1 == NUM_DIV/2 - 1) begin
                    cnt1 <= 0;
                end else begin
                    cnt1 <= cnt1 + 1;
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Counter for tracking falling edge clock cycles
        always @(negedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                cnt2 <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt2 == NUM_DIV/2 - 1) begin
                    cnt2 <= 0;
                end else begin
                    cnt2 <= cnt2 + 1;
                end

        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                clk_div1 <= 0;

                if (cnt1 >= NUM_DIV/2) begin
                    clk_div1 <= ~clk_div1;
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Clock divider for negative edge
        always @(negedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                clk_div2 <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt2 >= NUM_DIV/2) begin
                    clk_div2 <= ~clk_div2;
                end
            end
        end
